record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: In a symmetric space, is every Killing tensor a sum of symmetr ic products of Killing vectors? Equivalently, is it true that the algebra of all pol ynomial integrals of the geodesic flow in a symmetric space is generated by linear integrals? Note that for general metrics the answer is clearly negative: ther e exist metrics admitting nontrivial Killing tensors and no Killing vectors. For constant curvature space s, the answer is positive [212]. 3.2 Superintegrable systems Recall that a natural Hamiltonian system is superintegrable, if it admits more functionally independent integrals (of some special form) than the dimension of the manifold ( in addition, one usually assumes that common level surfaces of these integrals are isotropic subma nifolds in T ∗ M ). A system is called maximally superintegrable, if the number of functionally independent integrals is 2 n - 1, which is the maximal number for an n-dimensional manifold. An interesting and well-studied class of superintegrable natural Ha miltonian systems consists of geodesic flows of Zoll metrics. Recall that a Riemannian metric (on a closed man ifold) is called a Zoll metric if all its geodesics are closed, see e.g. [11]. In this case, the Hamiltonian flow can be viewed as a symplec- tic action of S1, the orbit space is an orbifold, and any function defined on this orbif old is an integral. Notice that locally, near almost every point, each natural Hamiltonia n system is superintegrable. It is therefore standard to consider superintegrability in the class of in tegrals of a special form, typically, polynomial in momenta. Then, superintegrability is a nontrivial condit ion on the system, even locally. In dimension two, superintegrable systems with quadratic integrals were locally essentially described in [57]. Superintegrable systems with one linear and one cubic integral were described in [162]; the 12 methods can be generalised for the case when one integral is linear a nd the second of arbitrary degree, see e.g. [218].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian symmetric space. A Killing vector field on $M$ is a vector field whose flow consists of isometries; equivalently, a vector field $X$ with $\mathcal{L}_X g = 0$. A symmetric Killing tensor of degree $k$ on $M$ is a symmetric $(0,k)$-tensor field $K$ satisfying the Killing equation $\operatorname{Sym}(\nabla K)=0$ (equivalently, the function $(x,p)\mapsto K_x(p,\dots,p)$ on $T^*M$ is a polynomial integral, of degree $k$ in the momenta, of the geodesic flow of $g$). The symmetric product of two symmetric Killing tensors is again a symmetric Killing tensor, so the space of all symmetric Killing tensors carries the structure of a graded commutative algebra.

Question: For every Riemannian symmetric space $(M,g)$, is every symmetric Killing tensor on $M$ expressible as a finite sum of symmetric products of Killing vector fields? Equivalently, is the algebra of polynomial-in-momenta integrals of the geodesic flow on $M$ generated by the linear integrals (those arising from Killing vector fields)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is answered in the negative for general Riemannian symmetric spaces. While decomposability of Killing tensors into symmetric products of Killing vectors holds on spaces of constant curvature (and on complex projective spaces), recent work exhibits explicit quadratic Killing tensors on the quaternionic projective spaces and on the Cayley projective plane that are not polynomials in Killing vector fields. This completes the classification of quadratic Killing tensor fields on rank-one Riemannian symmetric spaces and refutes the general decomposability conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Quadratic Killing tensors on symmetric spaces which are not generated by Killing vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Quadratic Killing tensor fields on quaternionic projective space and Cayley projective space are spanned by indecomposable ones and decomposable ones.
status_evidence.claim: There exist quadratic Killing tensors on the quaternionic projective spaces and Cayley projective plane that are not generated by Killing vector fields, providing a negative answer to the question for general symmetric spaces.

status_evidence.title: On Killing tensors on Riemannian symmetric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every Killing tensor field on spaces of constant curvature and on complex projective space can be decomposed into the sum of symmetric tensor products of Killing vector fields; this is not shared by all Riemannian symmetric spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Decomposability holds on constant curvature spaces and complex projective spaces but fails on other symmetric spaces.
